result.report:
PASS for the stated real-coefficient, finite weighted-tree cylinder theorem. The proof establishes an actual real-PAPC raw envelope, bounded reference difference, finite rational spatial domains and contact support for the full recursive measure. Cycles and the original classification remain open. No earlier verdict, compilation result or finite diagnostic is needed for this conclusion.

I checked the source conventions against the March 10 PDF of [BMPS v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1), including the rational-endpoint PCC definition, primitive quotient normals, local-cycle PAPC tests, growth class, regularization, envelope and recursive measure definitions. I also read the relevant refinement and commutativity proofs and Proposition 6.13’s locality invocation. [Allermann–Rau, Proposition 3.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0709.3705v3) concerns integral-slope rational functions; it does not itself grant the real-coefficient extension. The supplied argument proves that extension directly. These source checks verify conventions rather than supply an indispensable external theorem, so premises and passages are empty.

The divisor reconstruction is valid. Changes of normal lift cancel tangentially, and the three refinement cases exhaust the possible dimensions of the minimal old face. After quotienting a codimension-two face, saturation is preserved. Writing u_s=b u_r+χv correctly gives the primitive normal class u_s/χ modulo the ray tangent. Substitution of balancing cancels the vector terms pairwise; equation (5), including its final tangential term, is symmetric. Thus balancing, locality, refinement independence and commutativity hold for real weights and coefficients. The product calculation retains the full normalization 2^d d!c.

The convex preliminaries provide the facts actually needed: rational point/ray generation for pointed cells, closedness of finitely generated polyhedra with real heights, continuous completion of rational Jensen data and affine supports for finite convex functions. Their supplied derivations are sufficient; no additional convex theorem is required.

The tree lift preserves the exact geometric and lattice data. Positivity of the sole local relation forces the full direction kernel to be one-dimensional. Each attachment identifies a primitive edge vector and adds a free lattice complement, preserving saturation of both old and new vertex lattices. Suppressing bivalent vertices is reversible and preserves their positions, primitive parameters, weights and rational subdivisions. The germwise maps preserve arbitrary rational cells, PCC incidences and barycentres, saturated tangent lattices, local cycles and recursive divisors. The rank calculation and weighted leaf relation imply a full-dimensional leaf simplex containing zero in its interior; far rational leaf endpoints consequently provide the ambient convex-hull bounds used later.

Lemma 1 establishes endpoint agreement and finite outgoing derivatives before constructing supports. The weighted vertex inequality excludes a derivative of −∞ because every other outgoing derivative has a finite upper bound. At each descendant, the required child-slope sum is no greater than the sum of the available upper bounds. The recursively chosen slopes therefore define compatible local linear forms and one global affine minorant, including on remote unbounded portions.

Lemma 2 handles raw competitors without assuming continuity. For each partial Legendre slope p, the rational-coefficient cylinder tests give the required inequalities for k_p. Finiteness propagates from one rational centre to every rational graph point: same-edge combinations reach endpoints, and vertex combinations with coefficients proportional to w_e/t_e reach arbitrary incident endpoints. A finite centre cannot admit an endpoint infimum of −∞. Slice subgradients and Lemma 1 then produce touching ambient affine minorants. Far-leaf convex combinations bound their supremum everywhere. Shrinking rational simplices, with actual real barycentric coefficients, establish majorization at every real carrier point; continuous upper bounds pass by rational density.

The obstacle epigraph construction yields a closed polyhedron K with full spatial projection and finite lower fibres, bounded below by the convex extension of γ−C. Its lower function H is the greatest ambient convex minorant. Lemma 2 bounds every raw competitor by H, while H restricted to the carrier is itself admissible. This proves the exact raw envelope identity and γ−C≤P≤γ+C. Rational domains follow separately: every lower face uses a subset of generators with rational spatial coordinates, so its spatial projection is rational despite arbitrary real heights. Supporting planes also prove nonnegativity against every local nonnegative real cycle in every positive dimension. Hence all recursive divisors are balanced and nonnegative, and P+1/j supplies the claimed uniform decreasing real regularization.

The contact proof establishes both vanishing antecedents. At a noncontact atom, a generator representation gives a nonzero rational space L annihilated by all active-slope differences. If any graph term is nonzero, the independent branch complements force each branch sum to be b_e v_e. The constructed positive branch functional gives b_e≥0, and the unique local relation gives b_e=cw_e with c>0. The corresponding full-vector sums lie in L∩W_q and project onto all of S_q. Therefore the residual germ factors through a rational quotient of dimension at most m<d. The quotient-skeleton induction kills the entire d-fold divisor. If every graph term is zero, L is a nonzero subspace of E shared by the carrier and function fans; retaining this lineality leaves no zero-dimensional face, so the full top coefficient again vanishes. These alternatives include junctions, bounded-edge interiors, unbounded edges and all affine-coordinate faces. Finite atomicity then gives contact support and the zero integral, componentwise.

The triangular calculation correctly demonstrates failure of the proposed unclosed lift, without asserting an envelope counterexample.
